name: Tan Sitong 譚嗣同
credit: Photograph of Tan Sitong, c. 1898 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Tan Sitong (譚嗣同, 1865–1898), born in Liuyang, Hunan, was a Chinese scholar, philosopher and political reformer, author of the treatise Renxue (An Exposition of Benevolence).

He took part in the Hundred Days' Reform of 1898 under the Guangxu Emperor. When the Empress Dowager Cixi ended the reform in a coup, he refused to flee and was executed in Beijing on 28 September 1898, one of the 'Six Gentlemen' of the reform.
The four-line poem preserved here is the one traditionally said to have been written on the wall of his prison cell before his death.

poems.title: 獄中題壁 (Yu zhong ti bi)
poems.author: Tan Sitong 譚嗣同
poems.text:
望門投止思張儉，
忍死須臾待杜根。
我自橫刀向天笑，
去留肝膽兩崑崙。
